scope_note: Project-scoped direct-evidence account for Google's Lenoir data-center campus in Caldwell County, North Carolina. Fifty-one observations are added: thirty-eight reported actuals and thirteen source projections. County principal-taxpayer values are separate Google business-personal and Tapaha Dynamics real-property stocks and are not tax bills, payments, investment, or mutually overlapping components; modeled same-year sums remain outside canonical evidence. Investment announcements overlap across phases and must not be summed, the 2024 Project Cardinal and LNR4A scopes may overlap, the 2026 billion-dollar announcement may include both, solar capacity is off-site nameplate rather than campus load, and water values are campus/state-reporting-boundary figures without a building allocation. Supplier payments, actual operating payroll, complete local tax receipts, utility bills, electricity use, same-scope marginal public-service costs, and causal county outcomes remain unresolved rather than zero.

project_updates.title: Campus boundary and chronology resolved
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: IM3 campus inventory, Google location and opening pages, NC Commerce expansion history, City/County Project Cardinal records, air permits, contractor records, and exact 708 Lynhaven Drive/LNR4A/Project Cardinal queries. The selected object is the Google-operated Lenoir campus at 708 Lynhaven Drive, including multiple buildings and later adjacent expansion parcels; it is not a single building, the off-site solar plant, Google's Durham office, or the statewide portfolio. Google opened the first data center in May 2008 after the 2007 announcement; a second building served traffic by 2013, and later public records document LNR4A and Project Cardinal expansion work.
project_updates.project_description: Google operates a multi-building data-center campus at 708 Lynhaven Drive in Lenoir, Caldwell County, with Tapaha Dynamics holding associated real property. Announced in 2007, the first data center opened in May 2008 and a second building was serving traffic by 2013. Public records document later campus expansion phases, including LNR4A construction and the adjacent Project Cardinal parcels, while off-site solar remains supporting infrastructure rather than part of the campus boundary.

project_updates.title: Assessor and tax-record audit separates recurring stocks and flows
project_updates.notes: Official routes checked: Caldwell County GIS owner/address/PIN search; County ACFR principal-taxpayer tables for FY2007-2025; City of Lenoir tax-payment guidance, MyGovHub/QuickPay routing, budgets and ACFRs; exact Google, Tapaha Dynamics, 708 Lynhaven, 914 Virginia, 919 Fairview, parcel 06 162 1 1A/NCPIN 2748394394 and parcel 06 162 1 1C/NCPIN 2748287853 queries. Twelve paired Google/Tapaha assessed-value years were recovered; FY2012, FY2014 and FY2022 paired tables were not located. The public portals did not expose a complete account-level bill/payment history without unavailable account or mailing credentials. Assessed values are stocks, not taxes or investment; City GASB 77 abatements are flows and remain separate.

project_updates.title: City abatement audit resolves seven realized annual amounts
project_updates.notes: City ACFR GASB 77 notes were checked for FY2017-2025 through the Finance archive, direct archive-item URLs, and North Carolina Treasurer LG Reports. FY2018, FY2019, FY2020, and FY2022-FY2025 report Technology Business taxes abated; FY2021 remained inaccessible in the public text routes and is not interpolated. The notes do not name the taxpayer, so attribution is based on the separately published Google/Tapaha agreement and is disclosed in every record. Budget refund projections of $4.7 million and $4.6 million are not substituted for actuals. County abatements, gross taxes paid, recipient distributions, and a same-scope fiscal net remain unavailable.

project_updates.title: Incentive, water-agreement, bond and compliance search
project_updates.notes: Official sources checked: October 22, 2024 joint agenda and minutes; City and County agenda archives; budgets, audits and capital schedules; NC Commerce JDIG and grant-report routes; NC legislative sales-tax statutes; exact Project Cardinal, Tapaha, Google, economic development agreement, clawback, annual grant, bond, debt, compliance and $6,880,000 searches. The executed agreement requires at least $600 million and 30 full-time jobs within five years and offers 20 annual grants equal to 50% of real-property and 85% of equipment/personal-property taxes, subject to reductions and clawback. No Project Cardinal grant has yet been observed. The water agreement fixes a $6,880,000 reserve fee and prevailing bulk rates, but no receipt, meter, invoice, payment, or consumption schedule was found.

project_updates.title: Planning, permit, contractor and supplier search
project_updates.notes: Repositories checked: City/County agenda engineering attachments, NC Labor elevator registry, NC licensing and permit search results, H. J. Russell project portfolio, Truland references, ACS 2026 nonfinancial report, and exact LNR4/LNR4A/address/parcel/contractor queries. LNR4A is publicly linked to Google and the contractor reports a $510.7 million project value, 295,324 square feet, two data halls and 80 MW design capacity. The value is retained as a source projection, not paid cost. No invoices, subcontract values, vendor payments, local purchase share, supplier geography, worker count, payroll or completed cost were found; supplier contribution remains an explicit gap.

project_updates.title: Air, environmental and compliance record audit
project_updates.notes: NC DEQ/EPA air-permit review and issued permit were checked for Facility ID 1400204, application 1400204.24A, permit 09733T10, renewal 1400204.25A, 708 Lynhaven, generators, Title V, PSD, emissions, inspection and enforcement terms. The permit resolves 163 authorized emergency generators. The review reports 2019-2023 actual pollutants and an August 2024 late-report notice resolved in December 2024, but no monetary penalty or compliance cost. Missing canonical pollutant metrics are proposed separately; generator capacity, runtime, fuel use, operating cost and selected-building allocation remain unresolved.

project_updates.title: Water, sewer, electricity and utility audit
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Google 2024 impact and 2025 environmental reports; City public-utilities reports, water/wastewater budgets and rates; the 2017 and 2024 water-allocation agreements; Duke Energy Green Source Rider materials and NCUC orders; NC DEQ/EPA water and air routes. The 2024 report supplies 351.7 million gallons withdrawn, 23.9 million gallons discharged and 327.8 million gallons consumed at Lenoir; the impact study supplies 320.5 million gallons consumed in 2022 and 336.8 million in 2023. Only withdrawal has an adopted direct metric. No customer meter, bill, tariff determinants, annual kWh, campus MW load, sewer bill, peak demand, interconnection cost or public-utility capital allocation was found. Off-site 61 MW solar is not campus consumption.

project_updates.title: Workforce, payroll, procurement and training audit
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: original announcement coverage, NC Commerce, Google Careers and STAR program pages, NC Works/Commerce incentive and compliance routes, Caldwell County principal-employer tables, Caldwell Community College, Caldwell County Schools recipient pages, contractor records and exact jobs/payroll/wage/residence/training/procurement terms. The original 210-job and $48,300 average-salary plans and Project Cardinal's 30-job threshold are retained only as source projections. No realized annual-average FTE, Google payroll, benefits, contractor headcount, employee residence, occupation distribution, local hiring result, supplier transfer, or procurement ledger was found. A deterministic projected payroll scale is eligible; actual payroll and supplier models are rejected.

project_updates.title: Community-recipient search resolves local contributions
project_updates.notes: Operator, City, County, Caldwell Schools, Lenoir Housing Authority testimony, CISCC, CCC&TI, NCSSM and other recipient routes were checked for 2008-2026. Directly attributable local values retained are the greater-than-$1 million cumulative local total through 2013, $525,000 Gravity Games support for 2020-2023, a recipient-reported $50,000 Housing Authority grant in 2021, and the 2026 $2 million Energy Impact Fund, $100,000 City donation and $270,000 CISCC grant. Broader $1.7 million 2022-2023 North Carolina-community, $400,000 two-state Roanoke Cooperative, $125,000 statewide NCSSM, 512,000 trainees and 38,000 volunteer-hour figures are not assigned to the campus or summed with local awards.

project_updates.title: County outcome and public-cost candidate audit
project_updates.notes: BLS QCEW and BEA county panels, Census population context, City/County budgets and ACFRs, development records and service departments were reviewed over 2001-2025. A 2008 opening anchor permits descriptive matched-county employment and wage comparisons using 2001-2007 pretrends and 2024 outcomes. The analogous GDP result is rejected because the national matched estimate is -21.579900% while the North Carolina-only sensitivity is +4.719512%, a sign reversal. Employment and wage comparisons remain explicitly noncausal. No same-scope marginal police, fire, EMS, roads, water or administrative cost attributable to the campus was found, so no net fiscal or equal-cost threshold is asserted.

project_updates.title: Residual-gap model dispositions after candidate review
project_updates.notes: Retain twelve exact same-year Google-plus-Tapaha assessed-value aggregations; retain an exact 2007 projected annual payroll product; retain three water-consumption carry-through estimates with source-rounding bands; retain descriptive matched-county employment and wage comparisons with national K3/K5/K10, North Carolina K5 and leave-one-out sensitivity. Reject supplier/local-purchase and construction payroll models because no paid eligible base or geography exists; reject electricity-use/cost because PUE and solar capacity are not load; reject tax-receipt, net-fiscal and public-cost break-even models because gross project receipts, recipient distributions and same-scope marginal costs are absent; reject the GDP comparison for sign instability; reject Deloitte's statewide IMPLAN effects as already-modeled wider-scope outputs; and reject social-return scaling as directional and program-specific.
